headline: Former army officer Khandaker Abdul Hafiz arrested over anti-state activities and BDR massacre allegations
summary: The Dhaka Metropolitan Police's Detective Branch has taken retired major Khandaker Abdul Hafiz into custody. He faces allegations of involvement in activities against state security and the 2009 BDR massacre.
details: The Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s Detective Branch (DB) has arrested retired major Khandaker Abdul Hafiz. He faces serious allegations of involvement in activities against state security and the BDR massacre.
DB chief Shafiqul Islam confirmed the arrest to bdnews24.com on Sunday morning, stating that Hafiz is currently in DB custody.

DMP Deputy Commissioner (Media) Aktar Hossain added that Hafiz was taken into custody from Banani and is undergoing questioning. A case could be filed against him based on the anti-state activity allegations.

Before the ninth parliamentary election on September 6, 2008, Hafiz and several other former military officers formally joined the Awami League. They did so by presenting flowers to the party’s then acting president, Zillur Rahman.

headline: 30 garment factories suspend operation in Ashulia as new wage board is formed
summary: The Labour and Employment Minister announced the formation of a wage board today to review the minimum wage structure for garment workers, urging them to end their agitation and return to work.
details: Labour and Employment Minister Ariful Haque Choudhury announced the formation of a wage board to review the minimum wage structure for garment workers. He urged workers to end their agitation and return to work.

The announcement followed a meeting in Dhaka with representatives from the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) and Bangladesh Knitwear Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BKMEA). Both associations accepted the workers' demand for a wage board and agreed to coordinate with factory owners to clear outstanding wages.

The minister warned that factory closures and vandalism could harm the garment industry, disrupting production and supply chains, which might ultimately affect workers' wages. He also alleged that outsiders were instigating workers at some factories.

BGMEA Vice-president Md Rezwan Selim welcomed the move, stating the desire for a wage board to increase workers' wages. Nazma Akter, president of Sommilito Garments Sramik Federation, urged the government to form the wage board immediately to recommend a new pay structure.

Workers' living costs have significantly risen due to high inflation, impacting house rent, transport, and gas bills. The latest minimum wage for garment workers, fixed at Tk 12,500, took effect in December 2023 and is due for review this December.

The amended labour law requires wages across sectors to be reviewed every three years to account for inflation. A six-member wage board, including representatives from the government, trade unions, factory owners, an economist, and an independent member, typically recommends new minimum wages.
caption:
A new wage board is being formed to review the minimum wage for garment workers in Bangladesh, following widespread protests and the suspension of operations at 30 factories in Ashulia.

Labour and Employment Minister Ariful Haque Choudhury announced the formation of a wage board to review the minimum wage structure for garment workers. He urged workers to end their agitation and return to work.

The announcement followed a meeting in Dhaka with representatives from the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) and Bangladesh Knitwear Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BKMEA). Both associations accepted the workers' demand for a wage board and agreed to coordinate with factory owners to clear outstanding wages.

The minister warned that factory closures and vandalism could harm the garment industry, disrupting production and supply chains, which might ultimately affect workers' wages. He also alleged that outsiders were instigating workers at some factories.

BGMEA Vice-president Md Rezwan Selim welcomed the move, stating the desire for a wage board to increase workers' wages. Nazma Akter, president of Sommilito Garments Sramik Federation, urged the government to form the wage board immediately to recommend a new pay structure.

Workers' living costs have significantly risen due to high inflation, impacting house rent, transport, and gas bills. The latest minimum wage for garment workers, fixed at Tk 12,500, took effect in December 2023 and is due for review this December.

The amended labour law requires wages across sectors to be reviewed every three years to account for inflation. A six-member wage board, including representatives from the government, trade unions, factory owners, an economist, and an independent member, typically recommends new minimum wages.
